title: Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM): who gets which Viva feature?
summary: The policy controls, precedence, licensing requirement and limits are supported. The general statement that feature-level administrators can run the cmdlets needs narrowing: the reference for Get-VivaModuleFeatureEnablement requires the Global Administrators role.

claims.claim: VFAM policies enable or disable Microsoft 365 and Viva features or types of data processing for tenant users and groups.
claims.quote: You use policies to enable or disable specific features or types of data processing for users and groups in your tenant.

claims.claim: VFAM controls access to Insights features such as the Agent Dashboard.
claims.quote: | Insights | [Agent Dashboard](/en-us/viva/insights/advanced/admin/manage-settings-copilot-dashboard#enable-or-disable-the-agent-dashboard) | No | Global admin or AI admin | Viva Insights |

claims.claim: A policy applies to everyone, groups or users.
claims.quote: Policies are used to restrict or grant access to the specified feature for specific users, groups, or the entire tenant.

claims.claim: Subject to feature support, a policy can enable a feature for everyone in scope.
claims.quote: Enable the feature for everyone in the policy scope without considering user preference.

claims.claim: Subject to feature support, a policy can disable a feature for everyone in scope.

claims.claim: Subject to feature support, a policy can enable a feature with user opt-out.
claims.quote: Enable the feature for everyone in the policy scope while providing users the ability to opt out.

claims.claim: Subject to feature support, soft disable opts everyone out by default while allowing opt-in.
claims.quote: Enable the feature by opting out everyone in policy scope by default, while providing users the ability to opt in (soft disable).

claims.quote: Policies can be created and managed by an admin who has permissions to do so in the Microsoft 365 admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Some features accept only tenant-wide policies.
claims.quote: Some features only support policies that apply to the entire tenant, not specific users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The documented settings also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics, a Frontier preview, where applicable.
claims.quote: The settings described below also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier preview) where applicable.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: A user has one effective policy per feature.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each feature.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: User and group policies outrank the tenant policy and can allow access even when org-wide access is off.
claims.quote: Custom policies take precedence over your org-wide settings. For example, if you have organization-wide access turned off, a custom policy could still allow access for specific users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Policies assigned to a parent group reach users in nested groups.
claims.quote: When users are in nested groups and you apply access policies to the parent group, the users in the nested groups receive the policies.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Nested groups and their users must be created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: The nested groups and the users in those nested groups must be created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Without a user or group assignment, the org-wide policy or feature default applies.
claims.quote: If a user isn't assigned a policy as an individual or member of a group, the org-wide policy applies. It can be the default setting for the feature or a tenant-wide/org-wide policy created by the admin.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: At the same scope level, the most restrictive enablement policy wins.
claims.quote: Then within a single Policy Scope Level, the most restrictive Enablement Policy takes precedence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: defaults
claims.claim: The feature table does not list a default state; defaults must be checked per feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Viva feature access management" "feature table" "default". Read https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management: table columns are App, Feature, Control for user opt-out?, Who can manage access and ModuleID, with no default-state column.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app is on by default, including when no overriding policy is created.
claims.quote: The Viva Insights web app is on by default.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard is on by default as part of the Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: The Agent Dashboard is on by default as part of the Viva Insights web app.

claims.claim: Policy creation requires a supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite licence.
claims.quote:
Policy creation requires the following elements:
- A supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.

claims.claim: Microsoft links its Viva pricing page from the policy requirements.
claims.quote: A [supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-viva/pricing)

claims.claim: The VFAM pages publish no separate price or meter for creating or holding policies as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Viva feature access management" price meter policies billing. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management, https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/manage-access-policies and https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center; no policy price or meter is stated.

claims.claim: Policies do not grant access to otherwise unavailable features, as illustrated by Microsoft's EDU tenant example.
claims.quote: For example, if you have an EDU-based tenant, you can't use policies to gain access to features that aren't otherwise available to EDU tenants.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risks and limits: Updates overwrite the audience
claims.claim: Update values for UserIds, GroupIds or Everyone overwrite existing users or groups.
claims.quote: Values that you specify for the -UserIds and -GroupIds parameters or the -Everyone parameter overwrite any existing users or groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Updates overwrite the audience
claims.claim: Existing members omitted from an audience update are removed.
claims.quote: Not including existing users or groups in the command effectively removes those specific users or groups from the policy.

claims.claim: A feature permits up to 10 policies assigned to users and groups.
claims.quote: You can assign a maximum of 10 policies per feature to users and groups.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Small limits
claims.claim: Each policy can cover up to 20 users or groups in total.
claims.quote: You can specify a maximum of 20 total users or groups (20 users and no groups, 10 users and 10 groups, etc.).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Small limits
claims.claim: One additional tenant-wide policy per feature can be assigned using Everyone.
claims.quote: You can assign one additional policy per feature to the entire tenant by using the -Everyone parameter, which will function as a global default state for that feature across your organization.

claims.claim: Policy names must be unique.
claims.quote: Policy names must be unique.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Access policy changes take effect within 24 hours unless a feature documents otherwise.
claims.quote: Changes to access policies take effect for the user within 24 hours, unless noted for a specific feature.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Changes for Copilot in Viva Engage can take up to 48 hours.
claims.quote: Changes for Copilot in Viva Engage might take up to 48 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Group membership changes can take 24 hours to affect feature access.
claims.quote: When you add users or remove them from a Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft 365 Group, it can take 24 hours before changes to their feature access take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Opt-out choices reset
claims.claim: Fully enabling or disabling a feature resets the user's opt-in/out preference.
claims.quote: When an admin fully enables or disables a feature, the user's opt in/out preference resets to the default state.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Opt-out choices reset
claims.claim: Successive enablement changes under 24 hours apart might not reset preferences.
claims.quote: Avoid making changes to the enablement state for a feature less than 24 hours after making an initial change. Quick successive changes might not reset user opt in/out preferences.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Deleting a user identity in Entra ID deletes its VFAM user data.
claims.quote: When you delete user identities in Microsoft Entra ID, user data is also deleted from Viva feature access management.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: A user restored during the soft-deleted period needs policies reassigned.
claims.quote: If user identities are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period, the admin needs to reassign policies to the user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Deleted groups are removed from stored policies.
claims.quote: When groups in Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 are deleted, they're deleted from the stored policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Groups restored during the soft-deleted period need policies reassigned.
claims.quote: If groups are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period, the admin needs to reassign policies to the groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scope depends on the feature
claims.claim: Viva Insights web app auto-enablement supports only tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: This control supports tenant-level policies only, not user or group-level policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scope depends on the feature
claims.claim: User or group policies on the tenant-only auto-enablement feature have no effect.
claims.quote: User- and group-level policies aren't supported for this feature and will not take effect if used.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One switch can cover an app
claims.claim: Disabling the Viva Insights web app disables the whole app, including the Copilot Dashboard.
claims.quote: Turning this control off disables the entire app, which includes the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports, and advanced analysis and admin tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One switch can cover an app
claims.claim: Previous Copilot Dashboard access configurations now apply to the entire Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: If you previously removed access to the Copilot Dashboard using Copilot Dashboard feature access management control or PowerShell, those configurations now apply to the entire Viva Insights web app.

claims.claim: The described access controls are unavailable in GCC High.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: The described access controls are unavailable in DoD.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs GCC administrators to each app's documentation for availability.
claims.quote: For GCC (Government Community Cloud), see the documentation for your specific app for availability.

claims.claim: The on/off control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote:
Select Create a policy.
Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy.
Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone disables the selected feature tenant-wide.
claims.quote:
Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone
This example adds a policy for the Reflection feature in Viva Insights. The policy disables the feature for all users in the organization.

claims.claim: The audience control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Apply access settings to > Specific people and groups.
claims.quote: Select Everyone or Specific people and groups under Apply access settings to. If you didn't select Everyone, add the specific people and groups you want to apply the policy to.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false, GroupIds and UserIds creates a disabled policy for the selected groups and UPNs.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name UsersAndGroups -IsFeatureEnabled $false -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com,57680382-61a5-4378-85ad-f72095d4e9c3 -UserIds user1@contoso.com,user2@contoso.com

claims.claim: Everyone must not be combined with GroupIds or UserIds.
claims.quote: Don't use this switch with the GroupIds or UserIds parameters.

claims.claim: User opt-out is offered for supporting features at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote: Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature. Some features also allow the option for users to opt out.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $true and IsUserControlEnabled $true enables a feature with user opt-out where supported.
claims.quote:
$true: The feature is enabled by the policy.
$true: User control is enabled by the policy. Users can opt out of the feature.

claims.claim: User-control policies apply only to features supporting those controls.
claims.quote: Only features that allow admins to enable and disable user controls by policy can use this parameter.

claims.claim: Adding IsUserOptedInByDefault $false sets soft disable on a supported enabled user-control policy.
claims.quote: $false: By default, users are opted out by the policy if the user hasn't set a preference.

claims.claim: IsUserOptedInByDefault requires IsUserControlEnabled $true.
claims.quote: This parameter can be set only when the IsUserControlEnabled parameter is set to $true.

claims.claim: An existing policy is edited at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > More actions > Edit policy.
claims.quote:
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu.
Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access.
Select the vertical ellipses (More actions) and choose Edit policy.

claims.claim: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, PolicyId and GroupIds changes an existing policy's group audience.
claims.quote: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com

claims.claim: Deletion is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > policy > Delete policy.
claims.quote:
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu.
Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access.
Select the policy you'd like to delete.
Select Delete policy.

claims.claim: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId and PolicyId deletes the policy.
claims.quote: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard policy route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft Viva > Viva Insights > Set up and management > Access Management > Turn Advanced Insights on or off > Feature access management > Agent Dashboard > Add policy.

Under Access Management, select Turn Advanced Insights on or off.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId AgentDashboard -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables the Agent Dashboard tenant-wide.
claims.quote:
Example: Turn off the Agent Dashboard for all users in your tenant
ModuleId : VivaInsights
FeatureId : AgentDashboard
Name : DisableFeatureForAll
IsFeatureEnabled : false
Everyone
